Chapter 8: Measuring Impact—Evidence from the Field
At the end of the day, the real question is—does any of this actually work? Well, over the past decade, we've gathered more and more evidence that checklists, when they're done right, really do move the needle on safety, quality, and efficiency.
Take healthcare, for example. When surgical safety checklists started rolling out, something remarkable happened. One large study showed that in hospitals using just a simple, 19-item checklist, deaths after surgery dropped by more than a third. Major complications? They fell by nearly half.
And this wasn’t just at fancy hospitals with endless resources. Even places with limited equipment and staff saw these big improvements.
Now, if we look at aviation, the story gets even more compelling. Since pilots began relying on standardized checklists, fatal accident rates have dropped dramatically, even as planes and air traffic have gotten way more complex. When investigators look into near-misses or accidents, they almost always find that skipped or rushed checklists led to mistakes piling up. But when crews stick to the checklist? Problems get caught early, and everyone lands safely.
Construction teams have seen the benefits, too. Picture a massive skyscraper project—a place where there’s a million moving parts. Teams used daily checklists to track inspections, deliveries, and safety checks. The result? Work flowed more smoothly, there were fewer injuries, and the project wrapped up ahead of schedule.
But these aren’t just statistics. Every number represents a life saved, valuable resources protected, and teams getting the chance to do their best work.
So, what’s really behind this success? There are a few key things you’ll notice:
Consistency. Checklists make sure critical steps never get missed, even when the pressure’s on.
Transparency. They shine a light on the process, so if something goes off track, you can spot it early and fix it.
Accountability. With clear roles and expectations, everyone knows exactly what’s needed from them.
Now, let’s be real—checklists aren’t a magic fix for every problem. They work best alongside strong leadership, a culture that’s open to learning, and a team that’s always looking to get better.
But here’s the key takeaway: when you use them well, checklists offer a simple, scalable way to make even the most complex work safer and more reliable.
